argument_summary: Certification is supportable only as a disclosure-conditioned position, not as an unconditional claim that rollout controls cure the weakness. The admissible record supports three bounded points: aggregate readiness passed, deployment monitoring and rollback controls exist, and the e-commerce seller enforcement segment remains exposed and below target. Under that record, the defensible packet is certification with an explicit caveat that policy compliance depends on pre-launch model-card disclosure of the named limitation, affected use case, evaluation context, and monitoring controls; the same evidence does not support saying rollout controls alone satisfy policy.
claims_about_business_cost: No separate business-cost justification is needed to defend this narrowed position. The supportable argument is governance-based: use the existing readiness and monitoring evidence, narrow the certification theory, and avoid unnecessary escalation by treating disclosure as the operative condition rather than claiming controls alone are sufficient.
claims_about_policy: The policy text cuts against any claim that small-cohort rollout, dashboards, or rollback eliminate disclosure duties where the affected named use case remains exposed. The admissible evidence also shows there is no approved risk acceptance covering that exposure. On the current record, the compliant interpretation is therefore not unconditional certification, but certification on a caveated basis: readiness and monitoring support launch governance, while policy compliance for the unresolved limitation requires the disclosure predicate to be treated as mandatory before launch.
concessions: The current admissible record does not show that the required model-card disclosure has already been completed or approved.
The current admissible record does not support an unconditional certify_model recommendation.
The rollout plan does not exclude the affected e-commerce seller enforcement segment, so exposure remains live at launch.
The draft risk acceptance is not an adequate substitute because it is unsigned and does not address the exposed segment.
